+class SpanIndex:
+    """Index one source document against its parsed root in a single pass,
+    so every element in the tree resolves to its byte span without
+    rescanning the source per lookup - the identity-location counterpart
+    of element_span_by_identity, built once per document instead of once
+    per call.
+
+    One pre-order walk (root.iter()) assigns every element its ordinal
+    among same-tag elements, in the same left-to-right order a well-formed
+    document's own opening tags appear in source; one _TOKEN_RE scan then
+    collects the opening-tag offset of every non-closing tag occurrence in
+    document order. span_of resolves an element's offset by tag and
+    ordinal and returns element_span from there - the two passes together
+    replace element_span_by_identity's per-call tree walk plus per-call
+    text rescan.
+
+    The same walk that assigns ordinals also keeps a reference to every
+    walked element for this index's entire lifetime (self._elements). This
+    matters specifically under the lxml backend: an lxml Element is a
+    transient proxy over the underlying libxml2 tree, and once nothing
+    references a proxy it can be garbage-collected - after which CPython
+    may reuse its memory address for a brand-new, unrelated proxy object.
+    Keying solely on id(element) without retaining a reference would let a
+    later, different element be assigned the same id() as an
+    already-collected one, and span_of would then silently resolve to the
+    wrong (stale) ordinal for that address. Holding self._elements for as
+    long as this index is alive guarantees every id() this index has ever
+    recorded stays bound to the original element for the index's whole
+    lifetime, so a lookup can never be confused by address reuse.
+
+    element_span_by_identity stays in place and unchanged for now because
+    split.py still calls it at three sites; its removal is a later
+    migration, once split.py's last caller moves to this index, so the
+    package never sits in a state where a shipped module imports a
+    function that no longer exists.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, source: str, root) -> None:
+        self._source = source
+        self._elements: list = []
+        self._ordinal_by_id: dict[int, int] = {}
+        tag_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
+        for element in root.iter():
+            tag = element.tag
+            if not isinstance(tag, str):
+                continue  # skip comments/PIs, whose lxml .tag is a callable, not a name
+            self._elements.append(element)
+            ordinal = tag_counts.get(tag, 0)
+            self._ordinal_by_id[id(element)] = ordinal
+            tag_counts[tag] = ordinal + 1
+
+        offsets_by_tag: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
+        for token in _TOKEN_RE.finditer(source):
+            if token.group(1):  # a closing tag never starts a new element
+                continue
+            tag_name = token.group(2)
+            if tag_name is None:
+                continue
+            offsets_by_tag.setdefault(tag_name, []).append(token.start())
+        self._offsets_by_tag = offsets_by_tag
+
+    def span_of(self, element) -> Span:
+        """Return element's full byte span, resolved by its tag and
+        ordinal among same-tag elements rather than by rescanning source.
+        Raises ValueError naming the tag when element is absent from the
+        indexed tree, or when that tag's source occurrences run short of
+        its ordinal."""
+        tag_name = element.tag
+        ordinal = self._ordinal_by_id.get(id(element))
+        if ordinal is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"element <{tag_name}> is not part of the indexed tree")
+        offsets = self._offsets_by_tag.get(tag_name, [])
+        if ordinal >= len(offsets):
+            raise ValueError(f"could not locate occurrence {ordinal} of <{tag_name}> in source text")
+        return element_span(self._source, offsets[ordinal])
+
